steps.message:
`client.py` is shared. `scripts/export_prod.py` sets `REPORTS_BASE_URL=https://reports.example.com` and calls the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports`, so `verify=False` there disables certificate validation for the production nightly finance export too, not just staging — that makes those production calls silently accept any certificate (MITM-able on the network path), and it fails open with no error to notice.

The staging-only claim is about the staging cert; the code path isn't staging-only. I'd rather not flip it globally without your say-so.

steps.message:
**What changed** — `client.py` only, both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY`:

```python
VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE") or True
```

Default is `True`, so `scripts/export_prod.py` keeps full certificate validation against `reports.example.com`. Staging trusts its self-signed cert by pointing at the CA:

```bash
REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/staging-ca.pem python scripts/sync_staging.py
```

You need the staging CA cert in PEM form for that — `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect reports.staging.example:443 </dev/null` will dump it if you don't already have it on disk. If you'd rather not pass the env var each time, say so and I'll `setdefault` it in `sync_staging.py` at whatever path you keep the cert.

**Checks run:** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass; syntax parses. I did not make live HTTPS calls to either host, so the staging handshake against a real CA bundle is unverified.

If you did mean the literal `verify=False` on both calls and were waving off the production concern, tell me and I'll switch it — but that would turn off validation for the finance export too.
